conflicts.subject: post
conflicts.detail: Post primary keys differ (A: uuid, B: integer)
solutions: Pick one key type for the merged entity and re-key the other source's rows
Keep a legacy_id column holding the old key during migration
conflicts.recommended: Use one key type (uuid is usual for merged data) and add a legacy_id column while migrating

resolution.decision: uuid primary key for every post; B's integer ids kept in legacy_id (unique, nullable) during and after migration

conflicts.subject: GET /api/posts/{} response
conflicts.detail: GET /api/posts/{} response fields disagree (body: A text, B str; id: A uuid, B integer)
solutions: Define one request and response shape and convert at the edges
Version the endpoint if existing clients need the old shape
conflicts.recommended: One contract per endpoint, written into the API spec

resolution.decision: One contract: {id: uuid, body: text, status: pending|published|rejected, author: {id: uuid, display_name: text}, created_at}. No integer-id compatibility layer (no B API clients are known)

conflicts.subject: GET /api/posts/{}
conflicts.detail: GET /api/posts/{} uses different auth (A: cookie session, B: none)
solutions: Put every endpoint behind the one auth system the architecture chooses
conflicts.recommended: Same auth scheme for every endpoint

resolution.decision: One cookie-session auth; GET /api/posts/:id is public for published posts, author or moderator only for pending/rejected (404 otherwise)

conflicts.subject: model
conflicts.detail: Authorization models differ (A: role-based: member, moderator; requiresession / requiremoderator guards; B: roles user, admin carried in the token; no role checks seen in the api)
solutions: Choose one authorization model and express the others' rules in it
conflicts.recommended: One authorization model with one permission check function

resolution.decision: Role-based model with one can(user, action, resource) check used by every handler; actions: post.create, post.read_unpublished, moderation.list, moderation.decide

conflicts.subject: max-post-length
conflicts.detail: A limits a post body to 5000 characters (constant and DB check); B allows 10000. B posts between 5001 and 10000 characters would be rejected by A's constraint during migration.
solutions: Unified limit 10000 (widen A's check; no existing post rejected)
Unified limit 5000 and truncate or reject longer B posts (data loss)
5000 for new posts, longer legacy posts allowed through a legacy flag
conflicts.recommended: Unified limit 10000: widening loses nothing and moderators review every new post anyway

resolution.decision: Unified limit 10000 characters (server validation and DB check)

conflicts.subject: roles
conflicts.detail: Role sets differ (A: member, moderator; B: admin, user)
solutions: Map every source role to a unified role set and write the mapping down
Model special powers (such as approving) as permissions, not extra roles
conflicts.recommended: One role set plus explicit permissions; map every source role

resolution.decision: Unified roles member and moderator. Map A member->member, A moderator->moderator, B user->member, B admin->member (least privilege: admin had no observed powers); former B admins are listed for the user to promote by hand

conflicts.subject: /login
conflicts.detail: Route /login is used by A: A-S03, B: B-S02
solutions: Merge both screens into one page with sections
Move one to a different path
conflicts.recommended: One route per screen in the unified navigation

conflicts.subject: /posts
conflicts.detail: Route /posts is used by A: A-S01, B: B-S01
solutions: Merge both screens into one page with sections
Move one to a different path
conflicts.recommended: One route per screen in the unified navigation

conflicts.subject: session
conflicts.detail: Session mechanisms differ (A: server-side cookie session (req.session.userid); B: stateless jwt bearer token (no expiry seen))
solutions: Choose one session mechanism (http-only cookie sessions are the safer default for web apps)
Use tokens only where a client cannot hold cookies
conflicts.recommended: One session mechanism for the whole app

resolution.decision: Server-side session in an http-only, secure, same-site cookie; no bearer tokens

conflicts.subject: publish-policy
conflicts.detail: A holds every new post as pending until a moderator publishes it; B publishes every post immediately. B's existing posts were never moderated.
solutions: Pre-moderate every new post; migrate B's existing posts as published (grandfathered)
Pre-moderate every new post and push B's existing posts into the moderation queue
Publish immediately and moderate afterwards (drops A's rule)
conflicts.recommended: Pre-moderate every new post; migrate B's existing posts as published, since they are already public

resolution.decision: Every new post is pending until a moderator decides; B's existing posts migrate as published

conflicts.subject: user-accounts
conflicts.detail: B's users (integer ids, 'name', roles user/admin) author B's posts and must be merged into A's users (uuid, 'display_name', roles member/moderator). The same email may exist in both apps. Password hashing in both sources is unknown, so B's stored credentials may not verify in the unified app.
solutions: Re-key B users to uuid with legacy_id; name -> display_name; link accounts with the same email into A's record; force a password reset where hashes cannot be verified
Keep B users as separate accounts even when emails match (email must stay unique, so this fails)
conflicts.recommended: Re-key with legacy_id, map name to display_name, merge same-email accounts into A's record, and require a password reset for B accounts whose hash format is not supported

resolution.decision: Re-key B users to uuid with legacy_id; name -> display_name; same-email accounts merged into A's record; password reset required where B's hash format cannot be verified. Approved as a plan only; running it needs a separate approval

conflicts.subject: post.author_id
conflicts.detail: Post.author_id types differ (A: uuid, B: integer)
solutions: Choose the wider type and convert the narrower data
Split into two fields if they mean different things
conflicts.recommended: One type per field; convert in a migration

resolution.decision: author_id is uuid referencing users.id; B's integer author ids are rewritten through the user legacy_id map

conflicts.subject: post.author_id
conflicts.detail: A requires an author (author_id not null); B allows null author_id for anonymous posts. Anonymous posting (M08) was dropped, but B's existing anonymous posts still have no author.
solutions: Assign legacy anonymous posts to one reserved, sign-in-disabled system account and keep author_id not null
Make author_id nullable for legacy rows only
Do not migrate anonymous posts (data loss)
conflicts.recommended: Reserved system account 'Anonymous (OpenForum archive)' with sign-in disabled; author_id stays not null

resolution.decision: Legacy anonymous B posts are assigned to a reserved sign-in-disabled system account; author_id stays not null

conflicts.subject: GET /api/posts/{}
solutions: Keep one endpoint and adapt clients of the other
Keep both under different paths if they serve different needs
conflicts.recommended: One endpoint per job in the unified API

conflicts.subject: methods
conflicts.detail: Sign-in methods differ (A: email + credentials; B: email + password)
solutions: Offer the union of kept sign-in methods through one identity system
Drop sign-in methods no kept feature needs
conflicts.recommended: One identity system that offers the sign-in methods kept features need

resolution.decision: Email + password only, through the one identity system

conflicts.subject: b-token-signing-key
conflicts.detail: B signs JWTs with a hard-coded literal key and no expiry. B's token sign-in was dropped; any B tokens in the wild must stop working.
solutions: Do not reuse B's token code; B tokens become invalid at cut-over
Keep a temporary token bridge (would keep the weak key alive)
conflicts.recommended: No reuse of B's token code; B tokens are invalid after cut-over; the unified session secret comes only from configuration

resolution.decision: B's token code is not reused; B tokens are invalid at cut-over; session secret from configuration only

conflicts.subject: post
conflicts.detail: Post exists in A:Post, B:Post; fields not shared: status (only A)
solutions: Merge into one table holding the fields kept features need
Keep separate tables if the two only share a name, and rename one
conflicts.recommended: Merge into one entity; list every field's origin in architecture.json

resolution.decision: One posts table; status from A; B rows get status published (see publish-policy)
